personae.name: SEBASTIAN
personae.blurb: a young Gentleman, twin brother to Viola

personae.name: ANTONIO
personae.blurb: a Sea Captain, friend to Sebastian

personae.name: Lords
personae.blurb: Sailors, Officers, Musicians, and other Attendants

scenes.setting: An Apartment in the Duke’s Palace.

lines.text: Enter Orsino, Duke of Illyria, Curio, and other Lords; Musicians attending.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If music be the food of love, play on,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Give me excess of it; that, surfeiting,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The appetite may sicken and so die.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That strain again, it had a dying fall;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, it came o’er my ear like the sweet sound

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That breathes upon a bank of violets,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Stealing and giving odour. Enough; no more;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Tis not so sweet now as it was before.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O spirit of love, how quick and fresh art thou,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That notwithstanding thy capacity

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Receiveth as the sea, nought enters there,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of what validity and pitch soever,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But falls into abatement and low price

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Even in a minute! So full of shapes is fancy,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That it alone is high fantastical.

lines.speaker: CURIO
lines.text: Will you go hunt, my lord?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What, Curio?

lines.speaker: CURIO
lines.text: The hart.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why so I do, the noblest that I have.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, when mine eyes did see Olivia first,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Methought she purg’d the air of pestilence;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That instant was I turn’d into a hart,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And my desires, like fell and cruel hounds,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: E’er since pursue me. How now? what news from her?
Enter Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: So please my lord, I might not be admitted,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But from her handmaid do return this answer:

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: The element itself, till seven years’ heat,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Shall not behold her face at ample view;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But like a cloistress she will veiled walk,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And water once a day her chamber round

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With eye-offending brine: all this to season

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: A brother’s dead love, which she would keep fresh

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And lasting in her sad remembrance.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, she that hath a heart of that fine frame

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To pay this debt of love but to a brother,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How will she love, when the rich golden shaft

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hath kill’d the flock of all affections else

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That live in her; when liver, brain, and heart,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: These sovereign thrones, are all supplied and fill’d

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Her sweet perfections with one self king!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Away before me to sweet beds of flowers,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Love-thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Viola, a Captain and Sailors.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What country, friends, is this?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: This is Illyria, lady.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And what should I do in Illyria?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My brother he is in Elysium.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Perchance he is not drown’d. What think you, sailors?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: It is perchance that you yourself were sav’d.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: O my poor brother! and so perchance may he be.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: True, madam; and to comfort you with chance,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Assure yourself, after our ship did split,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: When you, and those poor number sav’d with you,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Hung on our driving boat, I saw your brother,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Most provident in peril, bind himself,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: (Courage and hope both teaching him the practice)

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: To a strong mast that liv’d upon the sea;

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Where, like Arion on the dolphin’s back,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: I saw him hold acquaintance with the waves

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: So long as I could see.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For saying so, there’s gold!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Mine own escape unfoldeth to my hope,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Whereto thy speech serves for authority,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The like of him. Know’st thou this country?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Ay, madam, well, for I was bred and born

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Not three hours’ travel from this very place.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Who governs here?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: A noble duke, in nature as in name.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What is his name?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Orsino.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Orsino! I have heard my father name him.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: He was a bachelor then.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And so is now, or was so very late;

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: For but a month ago I went from hence,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And then ’twas fresh in murmur, (as, you know,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: What great ones do, the less will prattle of)

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: That he did seek the love of fair Olivia.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What’s she?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: A virtuous maid, the daughter of a count

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: That died some twelvemonth since; then leaving her

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: In the protection of his son, her brother,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Who shortly also died; for whose dear love

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: They say, she hath abjur’d the company

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And sight of men.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: O that I served that lady,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And might not be delivered to the world,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Till I had made mine own occasion mellow,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What my estate is.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: That were hard to compass,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Because she will admit no kind of suit,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: No, not the Duke’s.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: There is a fair behaviour in thee, Captain;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And though that nature with a beauteous wall

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Doth oft close in pollution, yet of thee

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I will believe thou hast a mind that suits

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: With this thy fair and outward character.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I pray thee, and I’ll pay thee bounteously,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Conceal me what I am, and be my aid

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For such disguise as haply shall become

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The form of my intent. I’ll serve this duke;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Thou shalt present me as an eunuch to him.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: It may be worth thy pains; for I can sing,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And speak to him in many sorts of music,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That will allow me very worth his service.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What else may hap, to time I will commit;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Be you his eunuch and your mute I’ll be;

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: When my tongue blabs, then let mine eyes not see.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I thank thee. Lead me on.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Toby and Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What a plague means my niece to take the death of her brother thus? I

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: am sure care’s an enemy to life.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: By my troth, Sir Toby, you must come in earlier o’ nights; your cousin,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: my lady, takes great exceptions to your ill hours.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, let her except, before excepted.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ay, but you must confine yourself within the modest limits of order.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Confine? I’ll confine myself no finer than I am. These clothes are good

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: enough to drink in, and so be these boots too; and they be not, let

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: them hang themselves in their own straps.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: That quaffing and drinking will undo you: I heard my lady talk of it

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: yesterday; and of a foolish knight that you brought in one night here

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: to be her wooer.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Who? Sir Andrew Aguecheek?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ay, he.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: He’s as tall a man as any’s in Illyria.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: What’s that to th’ purpose?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, he has three thousand ducats a year.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ay, but he’ll have but a year in all these ducats. He’s a very fool,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: and a prodigal.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Fie, that you’ll say so! he plays o’ the viol-de-gamboys, and speaks

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: three or four languages word for word without book, and hath all the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: good gifts of nature.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: He hath indeed, almost natural: for, besides that he’s a fool, he’s a

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: great quarreller; and, but that he hath the gift of a coward to allay

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: the gust he hath in quarrelling, ’tis thought among the prudent he

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: would quickly have the gift of a grave.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: By this hand, they are scoundrels and substractors that say so of him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Who are they?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: They that add, moreover, he’s drunk nightly in your company.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: With drinking healths to my niece; I’ll drink to her as long as there

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: is a passage in my throat, and drink in Illyria. He’s a coward and a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: coystril that will not drink to my niece till his brains turn o’ the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: toe like a parish top. What, wench! _Castiliano vulgo:_ for here comes

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Sir Andrew Agueface.
Enter Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: AGUECHEEK
lines.text: Sir Toby Belch! How now, Sir Toby Belch?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Sweet Sir Andrew!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Bless you, fair shrew.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: And you too, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Accost, Sir Andrew, accost.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: What’s that?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: My niece’s chamber-maid.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Good Mistress Accost, I desire better acquaintance.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: My name is Mary, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Good Mistress Mary Accost,—

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: You mistake, knight: accost is front her, board her, woo her, assail

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: her.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: By my troth, I would not undertake her in this company. Is that the

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: meaning of accost?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Fare you well, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And thou let part so, Sir Andrew, would thou mightst never draw sword

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: again.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And you part so, mistress, I would I might never draw sword again. Fair

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: lady, do you think you have fools in hand?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Sir, I have not you by the hand.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Marry, but you shall have, and here’s my hand.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Now, sir, thought is free. I pray you, bring your hand to th’ buttery

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: bar and let it drink.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Wherefore, sweetheart? What’s your metaphor?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: It’s dry, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Why, I think so; I am not such an ass but I can keep my hand dry. But

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: what’s your jest?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: A dry jest, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Are you full of them?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ay, sir, I have them at my fingers’ ends: marry, now I let go your

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: hand, I am barren.
[_Exit Maria._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: O knight, thou lack’st a cup of canary: When did I see thee so put

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: down?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Never in your life, I think, unless you see canary put me down.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Methinks sometimes I have no more wit than a Christian or an ordinary

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: man has; but I am a great eater of beef, and I believe that does harm

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: to my wit.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: No question.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And I thought that, I’d forswear it. I’ll ride home tomorrow, Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Pourquoy_, my dear knight?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: What is _pourquoy?_ Do, or not do? I would I had bestowed that time in

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: the tongues that I have in fencing, dancing, and bear-baiting. O, had I

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: but followed the arts!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Then hadst thou had an excellent head of hair.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Why, would that have mended my hair?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Past question; for thou seest it will not curl by nature.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: But it becomes me well enough, does’t not?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Excellent, it hangs like flax on a distaff; and I hope to see a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: huswife take thee between her legs, and spin it off.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Faith, I’ll home tomorrow, Sir Toby; your niece will not be seen, or if

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: she be, it’s four to one she’ll none of me; the Count himself here hard

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: by woos her.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: She’ll none o’ the Count; she’ll not match above her degree, neither in

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: estate, years, nor wit; I have heard her swear’t. Tut, there’s life

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: in’t, man.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I’ll stay a month longer. I am a fellow o’ the strangest mind i’ the

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: world; I delight in masques and revels sometimes altogether.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Art thou good at these kick-shawses, knight?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: As any man in Illyria, whatsoever he be, under the degree of my

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: betters; and yet I will not compare with an old man.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What is thy excellence in a galliard, knight?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Faith, I can cut a caper.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And I can cut the mutton to’t.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And I think I have the back-trick simply as strong as any man in

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Illyria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Wherefore are these things hid? Wherefore have these gifts a curtain

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: before ’em? Are they like to take dust, like Mistress Mall’s picture?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why dost thou not go to church in a galliard, and come home in a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: coranto? My very walk should be a jig; I would not so much as make

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: water but in a sink-a-pace. What dost thou mean? Is it a world to hide

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: virtues in? I did think, by the excellent constitution of thy leg, it

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: was formed under the star of a galliard.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Ay, ’tis strong, and it does indifferent well in a dam’d-colour’d

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: stock. Shall we set about some revels?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What shall we do else? Were we not born under Taurus?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Taurus? That’s sides and heart.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: No, sir, it is legs and thighs. Let me see thee caper. Ha, higher: ha,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: ha, excellent!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Room in the Duke’s Palace.

lines.text: Enter Valentine and Viola in man’s attire.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If the duke continue these favours towards you, Cesario, you are like

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: to be much advanced; he hath known you but three days, and already you

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: are no stranger.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You either fear his humour or my negligence, that you call in question

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: the continuance of his love. Is he inconstant, sir, in his favours?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No, believe me.
Enter Duke, Curio and Attendants.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I thank you. Here comes the Count.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Who saw Cesario, ho?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: On your attendance, my lord, here.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Stand you awhile aloof.—Cesario,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou know’st no less but all; I have unclasp’d

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To thee the book even of my secret soul.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Therefore, good youth, address thy gait unto her,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be not denied access, stand at her doors,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And tell them, there thy fixed foot shall grow

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Till thou have audience.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Sure, my noble lord,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If she be so abandon’d to her sorrow

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As it is spoke, she never will admit me.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be clamorous and leap all civil bounds,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Rather than make unprofited return.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Say I do speak with her, my lord, what then?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O then unfold the passion of my love,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Surprise her with discourse of my dear faith;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: It shall become thee well to act my woes;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: She will attend it better in thy youth,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Than in a nuncio’s of more grave aspect.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I think not so, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Dear lad, believe it;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For they shall yet belie thy happy years,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That say thou art a man: Diana’s lip

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Is not more smooth and rubious; thy small pipe

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Is as the maiden’s organ, shrill and sound,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And all is semblative a woman’s part.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I know thy constellation is right apt

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For this affair. Some four or five attend him:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: All, if you will; for I myself am best

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: When least in company. Prosper well in this,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And thou shalt live as freely as thy lord,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To call his fortunes thine.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I’ll do my best

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: To woo your lady. [_Aside._] Yet, a barful strife!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Whoe’er I woo, myself would be his wife.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Maria and Clown.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nay; either tell me where thou hast been, or I will not open my lips so

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: wide as a bristle may enter, in way of thy excuse: my lady will hang

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: thee for thy absence.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Let her hang me: he that is well hanged in this world needs to fear no

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: colours.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Make that good.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: He shall see none to fear.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: A good lenten answer. I can tell thee where that saying was born, of I

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: fear no colours.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Where, good Mistress Mary?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: In the wars, and that may you be bold to say in your foolery.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Well, God give them wisdom that have it; and those that are fools, let

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: them use their talents.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Yet you will be hanged for being so long absent; or to be turned away;

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: is not that as good as a hanging to you?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Many a good hanging prevents a bad marriage; and for turning away, let

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: summer bear it out.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: You are resolute then?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Not so, neither, but I am resolved on two points.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: That if one break, the other will hold; or if both break, your gaskins

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: fall.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Apt, in good faith, very apt! Well, go thy way; if Sir Toby would leave

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: drinking, thou wert as witty a piece of Eve’s flesh as any in Illyria.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Peace, you rogue, no more o’ that. Here comes my lady: make your excuse

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: wisely, you were best.
[_Exit._]
Enter Olivia with Malvolio.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Wit, and’t be thy will, put me into good fooling! Those wits that think

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: they have thee, do very oft prove fools; and I that am sure I lack

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: thee, may pass for a wise man. For what says Quinapalus? Better a witty

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: fool than a foolish wit. God bless thee, lady!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Take the fool away.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Do you not hear, fellows? Take away the lady.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Go to, y’are a dry fool; I’ll no more of you. Besides, you grow

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: dishonest.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Two faults, madonna, that drink and good counsel will amend: for give

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the dry fool drink, then is the fool not dry; bid the dishonest man

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: mend himself, if he mend, he is no longer dishonest; if he cannot, let

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the botcher mend him. Anything that’s mended is but patched; virtue

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: that transgresses is but patched with sin, and sin that amends is but

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: patched with virtue. If that this simple syllogism will serve, so; if

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: it will not, what remedy? As there is no true cuckold but calamity, so

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: beauty’s a flower. The lady bade take away the fool, therefore, I say

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: again, take her away.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Sir, I bade them take away you.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Misprision in the highest degree! Lady, _cucullus non facit monachum:_

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: that’s as much to say, I wear not motley in my brain. Good madonna,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: give me leave to prove you a fool.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Can you do it?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Dexteriously, good madonna.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Make your proof.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I must catechize you for it, madonna. Good my mouse of virtue, answer

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: me.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Well sir, for want of other idleness, I’ll ’bide your proof.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Good madonna, why mourn’st thou?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Good fool, for my brother’s death.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I think his soul is in hell, madonna.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I know his soul is in heaven, fool.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: The more fool you, madonna, to mourn for your brother’s soul being in

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: heaven. Take away the fool, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What think you of this fool, Malvolio? doth he not mend?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Yes; and shall do, till the pangs of death shake him. Infirmity, that

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: decays the wise, doth ever make the better fool.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: God send you, sir, a speedy infirmity, for the better increasing your

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: folly! Sir Toby will be sworn that I am no fox; but he will not pass

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: his word for twopence that you are no fool.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How say you to that, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I marvel your ladyship takes delight in such a barren rascal; I saw him

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: put down the other day with an ordinary fool, that has no more brain

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: than a stone. Look you now, he’s out of his guard already; unless you

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: laugh and minister occasion to him, he is gagged. I protest I take

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: these wise men, that crow so at these set kind of fools, no better than

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: the fools’ zanies.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, you are sick of self-love, Malvolio, and taste with a distempered

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: appetite. To be generous, guiltless, and of free disposition, is to

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: take those things for bird-bolts that you deem cannon bullets. There is

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: no slander in an allowed fool, though he do nothing but rail; nor no

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: railing in a known discreet man, though he do nothing but reprove.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Now Mercury endue thee with leasing, for thou speak’st well of fools!
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Madam, there is at the gate a young gentleman much desires to speak

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: with you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: From the Count Orsino, is it?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: I know not, madam; ’tis a fair young man, and well attended.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Who of my people hold him in delay?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Sir Toby, madam, your kinsman.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Fetch him off, I pray you; he speaks nothing but madman. Fie on him!
[_Exit Maria._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Go you, Malvolio. If it be a suit from the Count, I am sick, or not at

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: home. What you will, to dismiss it.
[_Exit Malvolio._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Now you see, sir, how your fooling grows old, and people dislike it.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Thou hast spoke for us, madonna, as if thy eldest son should be a fool:

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: whose skull Jove cram with brains, for here he comes, one of thy kin

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: has a most weak _pia mater_.
Enter Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: By mine honour, half drunk. What is he at the gate, cousin?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: A gentleman.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A gentleman? What gentleman?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: ’Tis a gentleman here. A plague o’ these pickle-herrings! How now, sot?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Good Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Cousin, cousin, how have you come so early by this lethargy?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Lechery! I defy lechery. There’s one at the gate.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Ay, marry, what is he?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Let him be the devil an he will, I care not: give me faith, say I.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Well, it’s all one.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What’s a drunken man like, fool?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Like a drowned man, a fool, and a madman: one draught above heat makes

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: him a fool, the second mads him, and a third drowns him.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Go thou and seek the coroner, and let him sit o’ my coz; for he’s in

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: the third degree of drink; he’s drowned. Go, look after him.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: He is but mad yet, madonna; and the fool shall look to the madman.
[_Exit Clown._]
Enter Malvolio.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Madam, yond young fellow swears he will speak with you. I told him you

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: were sick; he takes on him to understand so much, and therefore comes

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: to speak with you. I told him you were asleep; he seems to have a

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: foreknowledge of that too, and therefore comes to speak with you. What

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: is to be said to him, lady? He’s fortified against any denial.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Tell him, he shall not speak with me.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Has been told so; and he says he’ll stand at your door like a sheriff’s

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: post, and be the supporter of a bench, but he’ll speak with you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What kind o’ man is he?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Why, of mankind.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What manner of man?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Of very ill manner; he’ll speak with you, will you or no.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Of what personage and years is he?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Not yet old enough for a man, nor young enough for a boy; as a squash

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: is before ’tis a peascod, or a codling, when ’tis almost an apple. ’Tis

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: with him in standing water, between boy and man. He is very

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: well-favoured, and he speaks very shrewishly. One would think his

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: mother’s milk were scarce out of him.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Let him approach. Call in my gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Gentlewoman, my lady calls.
[_Exit._]
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Give me my veil; come, throw it o’er my face.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: We’ll once more hear Orsino’s embassy.
Enter Viola.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The honourable lady of the house, which is she?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Speak to me; I shall answer for her. Your will?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Most radiant, exquisite, and unmatchable beauty,—I pray you, tell me if

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: this be the lady of the house, for I never saw her. I would be loath to

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: cast away my speech; for besides that it is excellently well penned, I

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: have taken great pains to con it. Good beauties, let me sustain no

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: scorn; I am very comptible, even to the least sinister usage.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Whence came you, sir?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I can say little more than I have studied, and that question’s out of

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: my part. Good gentle one, give me modest assurance, if you be the lady

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: of the house, that I may proceed in my speech.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Are you a comedian?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: No, my profound heart: and yet, by the very fangs of malice I swear, I

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: am not that I play. Are you the lady of the house?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If I do not usurp myself, I am.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Most certain, if you are she, you do usurp yourself; for what is yours

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: to bestow is not yours to reserve. But this is from my commission. I

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: will on with my speech in your praise, and then show you the heart of

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: my message.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Come to what is important in’t: I forgive you the praise.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Alas, I took great pains to study it, and ’tis poetical.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: It is the more like to be feigned; I pray you keep it in. I heard you

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: were saucy at my gates; and allowed your approach, rather to wonder at

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: you than to hear you. If you be mad, be gone; if you have reason, be

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: brief: ’tis not that time of moon with me to make one in so skipping a

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: dialogue.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Will you hoist sail, sir? Here lies your way.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: No, good swabber, I am to hull here a little longer. Some mollification

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: for your giant, sweet lady. Tell me your mind. I am a messenger.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Sure, you have some hideous matter to deliver, when the courtesy of it

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: is so fearful. Speak your office.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: It alone concerns your ear. I bring no overture of war, no taxation of

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: homage; I hold the olive in my hand: my words are as full of peace as

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: matter.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Yet you began rudely. What are you? What would you?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The rudeness that hath appeared in me have I learned from my

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: entertainment. What I am and what I would are as secret as maidenhead:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: to your ears, divinity; to any other’s, profanation.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Give us the place alone: we will hear this divinity.
[_Exit Maria._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Now, sir, what is your text?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Most sweet lady—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A comfortable doctrine, and much may be said of it. Where lies your

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: text?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: In Orsino’s bosom.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: In his bosom? In what chapter of his bosom?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: To answer by the method, in the first of his heart.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, I have read it; it is heresy. Have you no more to say?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Good madam, let me see your face.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Have you any commission from your lord to negotiate with my face? You

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: are now out of your text: but we will draw the curtain and show you the

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: picture. [_Unveiling._] Look you, sir, such a one I was this present.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Is’t not well done?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Excellently done, if God did all.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: ’Tis in grain, sir; ’twill endure wind and weather.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: ’Tis beauty truly blent, whose red and white

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Nature’s own sweet and cunning hand laid on.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Lady, you are the cruel’st she alive

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If you will lead these graces to the grave,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And leave the world no copy.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, sir, I will not be so hard-hearted; I will give out divers schedules

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: of my beauty. It shall be inventoried and every particle and utensil

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: labelled to my will: as, item, two lips indifferent red; item, two grey

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: eyes with lids to them; item, one neck, one chin, and so forth. Were

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: you sent hither to praise me?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I see you what you are, you are too proud;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But, if you were the devil, you are fair.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My lord and master loves you. O, such love

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Could be but recompens’d though you were crown’d

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The nonpareil of beauty!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How does he love me?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: With adorations, fertile tears,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: With groans that thunder love, with sighs of fire.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Your lord does know my mind, I cannot love him:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Yet I suppose him virtuous, know him noble,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Of great estate, of fresh and stainless youth;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: In voices well divulg’d, free, learn’d, and valiant,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And in dimension and the shape of nature,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A gracious person. But yet I cannot love him.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: He might have took his answer long ago.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If I did love you in my master’s flame,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: With such a suff’ring, such a deadly life,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: In your denial I would find no sense,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I would not understand it.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Why, what would you?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Make me a willow cabin at your gate,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And call upon my soul within the house;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Write loyal cantons of contemned love,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And sing them loud even in the dead of night;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Hallow your name to the reverberate hills,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And make the babbling gossip of the air

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Cry out Olivia! O, you should not rest

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Between the elements of air and earth,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But you should pity me.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: You might do much.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What is your parentage?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Above my fortunes, yet my state is well:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am a gentleman.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Get you to your lord;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I cannot love him: let him send no more,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Unless, perchance, you come to me again,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To tell me how he takes it. Fare you well:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I thank you for your pains: spend this for me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am no fee’d post, lady; keep your purse;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My master, not myself, lacks recompense.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Love make his heart of flint that you shall love,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And let your fervour like my master’s be

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Plac’d in contempt. Farewell, fair cruelty.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What is your parentage?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: ‘Above my fortunes, yet my state is well:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I am a gentleman.’ I’ll be sworn thou art;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Thy tongue, thy face, thy limbs, actions, and spirit,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Do give thee five-fold blazon. Not too fast: soft, soft!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Unless the master were the man. How now?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Even so quickly may one catch the plague?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Methinks I feel this youth’s perfections

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: With an invisible and subtle stealth

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To creep in at mine eyes. Well, let it be.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What ho, Malvolio!
Enter Malvolio.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Here, madam, at your service.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Run after that same peevish messenger

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: The County’s man: he left this ring behind him,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Would I or not; tell him, I’ll none of it.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Desire him not to flatter with his lord,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Nor hold him up with hopes; I am not for him.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If that the youth will come this way tomorrow,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I’ll give him reasons for’t. Hie thee, Malvolio.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Madam, I will.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I do I know not what, and fear to find

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Mine eye too great a flatterer for my mind.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Fate, show thy force, ourselves we do not owe.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What is decreed must be; and be this so!
[_Exit._]
Enter Antonio and Sebastian.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Will you stay no longer? Nor will you not that I go with you?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: By your patience, no; my stars shine darkly over me; the malignancy of

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: my fate might perhaps distemper yours; therefore I shall crave of you

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: your leave that I may bear my evils alone. It were a bad recompense for

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: your love, to lay any of them on you.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Let me know of you whither you are bound.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: No, sooth, sir; my determinate voyage is mere extravagancy. But I

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: perceive in you so excellent a touch of modesty, that you will not

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: extort from me what I am willing to keep in. Therefore it charges me in

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: manners the rather to express myself. You must know of me then,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Antonio, my name is Sebastian, which I called Roderigo; my father was

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: that Sebastian of Messaline whom I know you have heard of. He left

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: behind him myself and a sister, both born in an hour. If the heavens

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: had been pleased, would we had so ended! But you, sir, altered that,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: for some hour before you took me from the breach of the sea was my

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: sister drowned.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Alas the day!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: A lady, sir, though it was said she much resembled me, was yet of many

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: accounted beautiful. But though I could not with such estimable wonder

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: overfar believe that, yet thus far I will boldly publish her, she bore

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: a mind that envy could not but call fair. She is drowned already, sir,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: with salt water, though I seem to drown her remembrance again with

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: more.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Pardon me, sir, your bad entertainment.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: O good Antonio, forgive me your trouble.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: If you will not murder me for my love, let me be your servant.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: If you will not undo what you have done, that is, kill him whom you

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: have recovered, desire it not. Fare ye well at once; my bosom is full

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: of kindness, and I am yet so near the manners of my mother, that upon

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: the least occasion more, mine eyes will tell tales of me. I am bound to

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: the Count Orsino’s court: farewell.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: The gentleness of all the gods go with thee!

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I have many enemies in Orsino’s court,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Else would I very shortly see thee there:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But come what may, I do adore thee so,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That danger shall seem sport, and I will go.
[_Exit._]
Enter Viola; Malvolio at several doors.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Were you not even now with the Countess Olivia?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Even now, sir; on a moderate pace I have since arrived but hither.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: She returns this ring to you, sir; you might have saved me my pains, to

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: have taken it away yourself. She adds, moreover, that you should put

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: your lord into a desperate assurance she will none of him. And one

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thing more, that you be never so hardy to come again in his affairs,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: unless it be to report your lord’s taking of this. Receive it so.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: She took the ring of me: I’ll none of it.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Come sir, you peevishly threw it to her; and her will is it should be

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: so returned. If it be worth stooping for, there it lies in your eye; if

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: not, be it his that finds it.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I left no ring with her; what means this lady?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Fortune forbid my outside have not charm’d her!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: She made good view of me, indeed, so much,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That methought her eyes had lost her tongue,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For she did speak in starts distractedly.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: She loves me, sure, the cunning of her passion

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Invites me in this churlish messenger.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: None of my lord’s ring? Why, he sent her none.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am the man; if it be so, as ’tis,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Poor lady, she were better love a dream.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Disguise, I see thou art a wickedness

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Wherein the pregnant enemy does much.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: How easy is it for the proper false

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: In women’s waxen hearts to set their forms!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Alas, our frailty is the cause, not we,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For such as we are made of, such we be.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: How will this fadge? My master loves her dearly,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And I, poor monster, fond as much on him,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And she, mistaken, seems to dote on me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What will become of this? As I am man,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My state is desperate for my master’s love;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As I am woman (now alas the day!)

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What thriftless sighs shall poor Olivia breathe!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: O time, thou must untangle this, not I,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: It is too hard a knot for me t’untie!
[_Exit._]
Enter Sir Toby and Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Approach, Sir Andrew; not to be abed after midnight, is to be up

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: betimes; and _diluculo surgere_, thou know’st.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Nay, by my troth, I know not; but I know to be up late is to be up

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: late.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: A false conclusion; I hate it as an unfilled can. To be up after

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: midnight, and to go to bed then is early: so that to go to bed after

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: midnight is to go to bed betimes. Does not our lives consist of the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: four elements?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Faith, so they say, but I think it rather consists of eating and

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: drinking.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Th’art a scholar; let us therefore eat and drink.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Marian, I say! a stoup of wine.
Enter Clown.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Here comes the fool, i’ faith.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: How now, my hearts? Did you never see the picture of “we three”?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Welcome, ass. Now let’s have a catch.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: By my troth, the fool has an excellent breast. I had rather than forty

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: shillings I had such a leg, and so sweet a breath to sing, as the fool

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: has. In sooth, thou wast in very gracious fooling last night when thou

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: spok’st of Pigrogromitus, of the Vapians passing the equinoctial of

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Queubus; ’twas very good, i’ faith. I sent thee sixpence for thy leman.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Hadst it?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I did impeticos thy gratillity; for Malvolio’s nose is no whipstock. My

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: lady has a white hand, and the Myrmidons are no bottle-ale houses.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Excellent! Why, this is the best fooling, when all is done. Now, a

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: song.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come on, there is sixpence for you. Let’s have a song.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: There’s a testril of me too: if one knight give a—

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Would you have a love-song, or a song of good life?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: A love-song, a love-song.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Ay, ay. I care not for good life.
[_sings._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _O mistress mine, where are you roaming?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: O stay and hear, your true love’s coming,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: That can sing both high and low.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Trip no further, pretty sweeting.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Journeys end in lovers meeting,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Every wise man’s son doth know._

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Excellent good, i’ faith.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Good, good.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _What is love? ’Tis not hereafter,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Present mirth hath present laughter.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What’s to come is still unsure.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: In delay there lies no plenty,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Youth’s a stuff will not endure._

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: A mellifluous voice, as I am true knight.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: A contagious breath.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Very sweet and contagious, i’ faith.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: To hear by the nose, it is dulcet in contagion. But shall we make the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: welkin dance indeed? Shall we rouse the night-owl in a catch that will

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: draw three souls out of one weaver? Shall we do that?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And you love me, let’s do’t: I am dog at a catch.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: By’r lady, sir, and some dogs will catch well.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Most certain. Let our catch be, “Thou knave.”

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: “Hold thy peace, thou knave” knight? I shall be constrain’d in’t to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: call thee knave, knight.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Tis not the first time I have constrained one to call me knave. Begin,

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: fool; it begins “Hold thy peace.”

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I shall never begin if I hold my peace.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Good, i’ faith! Come, begin.
[_Catch sung._]
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: What a caterwauling do you keep here! If my lady have not called up her

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: steward Malvolio, and bid him turn you out of doors, never trust me.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: My lady’s a Cataian, we are politicians, Malvolio’s a Peg-a-Ramsey, and
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Three merry men be we._ Am not I consanguineous? Am I not

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: of her blood? Tilly-vally! “Lady”! _There dwelt a man in Babylon, Lady,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Lady._

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Beshrew me, the knight’s in admirable fooling.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Ay, he does well enough if he be disposed, and so do I too; he does it

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: with a better grace, but I do it more natural.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _O’ the twelfth day of December—_

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: For the love o’ God, peace!
Enter Malvolio.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: My masters, are you mad? Or what are you? Have you no wit, manners, nor

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: honesty, but to gabble like tinkers at this time of night? Do ye make

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: an ale-house of my lady’s house, that ye squeak out your coziers’

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: catches without any mitigation or remorse of voice? Is there no respect

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: of place, persons, nor time, in you?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: We did keep time, sir, in our catches. Sneck up!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir Toby, I must be round with you. My lady bade me tell you that,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: though she harbours you as her kinsman she’s nothing allied to your

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: disorders. If you can separate yourself and your misdemeanours, you are

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: welcome to the house; if not, and it would please you to take leave of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: her, she is very willing to bid you farewell.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Farewell, dear heart, since I must needs be gone._

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nay, good Sir Toby.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _His eyes do show his days are almost done._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Is’t even so?
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _But I will never die._
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _Sir Toby, there you lie._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: This is much credit to you.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Shall I bid him go?_
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _What and if you do?_
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Shall I bid him go, and spare not?_
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _O, no, no, no, no, you dare not._

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Out o’ tune? sir, ye lie. Art any more than a steward? Dost thou think,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Yes, by Saint Anne, and ginger shall be hot i’ the mouth too.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Th’art i’ the right. Go, sir, rub your chain with crumbs. A stoup of

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: wine, Maria!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Mistress Mary, if you prized my lady’s favour at anything more than

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: contempt, you would not give means for this uncivil rule; she shall

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: know of it, by this hand.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Go shake your ears.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Twere as good a deed as to drink when a man’s a-hungry, to challenge

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: him the field, and then to break promise with him and make a fool of

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Do’t, knight. I’ll write thee a challenge; or I’ll deliver thy

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: indignation to him by word of mouth.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Sweet Sir Toby, be patient for tonight. Since the youth of the Count’s

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: was today with my lady, she is much out of quiet. For Monsieur

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Malvolio, let me alone with him. If I do not gull him into a nayword,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: and make him a common recreation, do not think I have wit enough to lie

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: straight in my bed. I know I can do it.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Possess us, possess us, tell us something of him.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Marry, sir, sometimes he is a kind of Puritan.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: O, if I thought that, I’d beat him like a dog.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What, for being a Puritan? Thy exquisite reason, dear knight?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I have no exquisite reason for’t, but I have reason good enough.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: The devil a Puritan that he is, or anything constantly but a

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: time-pleaser, an affectioned ass that cons state without book and

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: utters it by great swarths; the best persuaded of himself, so crammed

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: (as he thinks) with excellencies, that it is his grounds of faith that

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: all that look on him love him. And on that vice in him will my revenge

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: find notable cause to work.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What wilt thou do?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: I will drop in his way some obscure epistles of love, wherein by the

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: colour of his beard, the shape of his leg, the manner of his gait, the

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: expressure of his eye, forehead, and complexion, he shall find himself

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: most feelingly personated. I can write very like my lady your niece; on

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: a forgotten matter we can hardly make distinction of our hands.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Excellent! I smell a device.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I have’t in my nose too.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: He shall think, by the letters that thou wilt drop, that they come from

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: my niece, and that she is in love with him.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: My purpose is indeed a horse of that colour.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And your horse now would make him an ass.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ass, I doubt not.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: O ’twill be admirable!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Sport royal, I warrant you. I know my physic will work with him. I will

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: plant you two, and let the fool make a third, where he shall find the

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: letter. Observe his construction of it. For this night, to bed, and

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: dream on the event. Farewell.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Good night, Penthesilea.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Before me, she’s a good wench.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: She’s a beagle true bred, and one that adores me. What o’ that?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I was adored once too.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Let’s to bed, knight. Thou hadst need send for more money.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: If I cannot recover your niece, I am a foul way out.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Send for money, knight; if thou hast her not i’ th’ end, call me cut.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: If I do not, never trust me, take it how you will.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, come, I’ll go burn some sack, ’tis too late to go to bed now.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, knight, come, knight.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Room in the Duke’s Palace.

lines.text: Enter Duke, Viola, Curio and others.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Give me some music. Now, good morrow, friends.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now, good Cesario, but that piece of song,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That old and antique song we heard last night;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Methought it did relieve my passion much,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: More than light airs and recollected terms

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of these most brisk and giddy-paced times.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Come, but one verse.

lines.speaker: CURIO
lines.text: He is not here, so please your lordship, that should sing it.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Who was it?

lines.speaker: CURIO
lines.text: Feste, the jester, my lord, a fool that the Lady Olivia’s father took

lines.speaker: CURIO
lines.text: much delight in. He is about the house.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Seek him out, and play the tune the while.
[_Exit Curio. Music plays._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Come hither, boy. If ever thou shalt love,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: In the sweet pangs of it remember me:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For such as I am, all true lovers are,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Unstaid and skittish in all motions else,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Save in the constant image of the creature

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That is belov’d. How dost thou like this tune?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: It gives a very echo to the seat

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Where love is throned.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou dost speak masterly.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My life upon’t, young though thou art, thine eye

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hath stayed upon some favour that it loves.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hath it not, boy?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: A little, by your favour.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What kind of woman is’t?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Of your complexion.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: She is not worth thee, then. What years, i’ faith?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: About your years, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Too old, by heaven! Let still the woman take

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: An elder than herself; so wears she to him,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So sways she level in her husband’s heart.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For, boy, however we do praise ourselves,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Our fancies are more giddy and unfirm,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: More longing, wavering, sooner lost and worn,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Than women’s are.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I think it well, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Then let thy love be younger than thyself,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Or thy affection cannot hold the bent:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For women are as roses, whose fair flower

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Being once display’d, doth fall that very hour.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And so they are: alas, that they are so;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: To die, even when they to perfection grow!
Enter Curio and Clown.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, fellow, come, the song we had last night.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Mark it, Cesario, it is old and plain;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The spinsters and the knitters in the sun,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And the free maids, that weave their thread with bones

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Do use to chant it: it is silly sooth,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And dallies with the innocence of love

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Like the old age.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Are you ready, sir?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay; prithee, sing.
[_Music._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The Clown’s song.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _    Come away, come away, death.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And in sad cypress let me be laid.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Fly away, fly away, breath;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I am slain by a fair cruel maid.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My shroud of white, stuck all with yew,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, prepare it!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My part of death no one so true

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Did share it._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _    Not a flower, not a flower sweet,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: On my black coffin let there be strown:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Not a friend, not a friend greet

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My poor corpse where my bones shall be thrown:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A thousand thousand sighs to save,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Lay me, O, where

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sad true lover never find my grave,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To weep there._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: There’s for thy pains.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No pains, sir; I take pleasure in singing, sir.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I’ll pay thy pleasure, then.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Truly sir, and pleasure will be paid one time or another.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Give me now leave to leave thee.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Now the melancholy god protect thee, and the tailor make thy doublet of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: changeable taffeta, for thy mind is a very opal. I would have men of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: such constancy put to sea, that their business might be everything, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: their intent everywhere, for that’s it that always makes a good voyage

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: of nothing. Farewell.
[_Exit Clown._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Let all the rest give place.
[_Exeunt Curio and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Once more, Cesario,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Get thee to yond same sovereign cruelty.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Tell her my love, more noble than the world,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Prizes not quantity of dirty lands;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The parts that fortune hath bestow’d upon her,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Tell her I hold as giddily as fortune;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But ’tis that miracle and queen of gems

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That nature pranks her in attracts my soul.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But if she cannot love you, sir?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I cannot be so answer’d.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Sooth, but you must.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Say that some lady, as perhaps there is,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Hath for your love as great a pang of heart

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As you have for Olivia: you cannot love her;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You tell her so. Must she not then be answer’d?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: There is no woman’s sides

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Can bide the beating of so strong a passion

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: As love doth give my heart: no woman’s heart

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So big, to hold so much; they lack retention.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Alas, their love may be called appetite,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: No motion of the liver, but the palate,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That suffer surfeit, cloyment, and revolt;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But mine is all as hungry as the sea,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And can digest as much. Make no compare

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Between that love a woman can bear me

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And that I owe Olivia.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Ay, but I know—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What dost thou know?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Too well what love women to men may owe.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: In faith, they are as true of heart as we.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My father had a daughter loved a man,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As it might be perhaps, were I a woman,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I should your lordship.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And what’s her history?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: A blank, my lord. She never told her love,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But let concealment, like a worm i’ th’ bud,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Feed on her damask cheek: she pined in thought,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And with a green and yellow melancholy

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: She sat like patience on a monument,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Smiling at grief. Was not this love, indeed?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: We men may say more, swear more, but indeed,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Our shows are more than will; for still we prove

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Much in our vows, but little in our love.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But died thy sister of her love, my boy?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am all the daughters of my father’s house,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And all the brothers too: and yet I know not.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Sir, shall I to this lady?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay, that’s the theme.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To her in haste. Give her this jewel; say

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My love can give no place, bide no denay.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Toby, Sir Andrew and Fabian.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come thy ways, Signior Fabian.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Nay, I’ll come. If I lose a scruple of this sport, let me be boiled to

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: death with melancholy.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Wouldst thou not be glad to have the niggardly rascally sheep-biter

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: come by some notable shame?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: I would exult, man. You know he brought me out o’ favour with my lady

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: about a bear-baiting here.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: To anger him we’ll have the bear again, and we will fool him black and

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: blue, shall we not, Sir Andrew?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And we do not, it is pity of our lives.
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Here comes the little villain. How now, my metal of India?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Get ye all three into the box-tree. Malvolio’s coming down this walk;

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: he has been yonder i’ the sun practising behaviour to his own shadow

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: this half hour: observe him, for the love of mockery; for I know this

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: letter will make a contemplative idiot of him. Close, in the name of

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: jesting! [_The men hide themselves._] Lie thou there; [_Throws down a

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: letter_] for here comes the trout that must be caught with tickling.
[_Exit Maria._]
Enter Malvolio.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ’Tis but fortune, all is fortune. Maria once told me she did affect me,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: and I have heard herself come thus near, that should she fancy, it

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: should be one of my complexion. Besides, she uses me with a more

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: exalted respect than anyone else that follows her. What should I think

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: on’t?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Here’s an overweening rogue!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: O, peace! Contemplation makes a rare turkey-cock of him; how he jets

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: under his advanced plumes!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Slight, I could so beat the rogue!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Peace, I say.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: To be Count Malvolio.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Ah, rogue!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Pistol him, pistol him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Peace, peace.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: There is example for’t. The lady of the Strachy married the yeoman of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: the wardrobe.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Fie on him, Jezebel!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: O, peace! now he’s deeply in; look how imagination blows him.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Having been three months married to her, sitting in my state—

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: O for a stone-bow to hit him in the eye!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Calling my officers about me, in my branched velvet gown; having come

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: from a day-bed, where I have left Olivia sleeping.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Fire and brimstone!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: O, peace, peace.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: And then to have the humour of state; and after a demure travel of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: regard, telling them I know my place as I would they should do theirs,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: to ask for my kinsman Toby.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Bolts and shackles!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: O, peace, peace, peace! Now, now.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Seven of my people, with an obedient start, make out for him. I frown

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: the while, and perchance wind up my watch, or play with some rich

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: jewel. Toby approaches; curtsies there to me—

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Shall this fellow live?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Though our silence be drawn from us with cars, yet peace!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I extend my hand to him thus, quenching my familiar smile with an

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: austere regard of control—

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And does not Toby take you a blow o’ the lips then?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Saying ‘Cousin Toby, my fortunes having cast me on your niece, give me

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: this prerogative of speech—’

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What, what?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘You must amend your drunkenness.’

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Out, scab!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Nay, patience, or we break the sinews of our plot.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Besides, you waste the treasure of your time with a foolish knight—’

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: That’s me, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘One Sir Andrew.’

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I knew ’twas I, for many do call me fool.
[_Taking up the letter._]

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: What employment have we here?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Now is the woodcock near the gin.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: O, peace! And the spirit of humours intimate reading aloud to him!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: By my life, this is my lady’s hand: these be her very C’s, her U’s, and

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: her T’s, and thus makes she her great P’s. It is in contempt of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: question, her hand.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Her C’s, her U’s, and her T’s. Why that?
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: _To the unknown beloved, this, and my good wishes._ Her very

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: phrases! By your leave, wax. Soft! and the impressure her Lucrece, with

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: which she uses to seal: ’tis my lady. To whom should this be?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: This wins him, liver and all.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: _    Jove knows I love,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: But who?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Lips, do not move,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: No man must know._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘No man must know.’ What follows? The numbers alter’d! ‘No man must

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: know.’—If this should be thee, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Marry, hang thee, brock!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: _    I may command where I adore,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: But silence, like a Lucrece knife,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: With bloodless stroke my heart doth gore;

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: M.O.A.I. doth sway my life._

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: A fustian riddle!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Excellent wench, say I.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘M.O.A.I. doth sway my life.’—Nay, but first let me see, let me see,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: let me see.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: What dish o’ poison has she dressed him!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And with what wing the staniel checks at it!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘I may command where I adore.’ Why, she may command me: I serve her,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: she is my lady. Why, this is evident to any formal capacity. There is

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: no obstruction in this. And the end—what should that alphabetical

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: position portend? If I could make that resemble something in me!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Softly! ‘M.O.A.I.’—

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: O, ay, make up that:—he is now at a cold scent.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Sowter will cry upon’t for all this, though it be as rank as a fox.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
