lines.text: ‘M’—Malvolio; ‘M!’ Why, that begins my name!

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Did not I say he would work it out? The cur is excellent at faults.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘M’—But then there is no consonancy in the sequel; that suffers under

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: probation: ‘A’ should follow, but ‘O’ does.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: And ‘O’ shall end, I hope.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Ay, or I’ll cudgel him, and make him cry ‘O!’

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: And then ‘I’ comes behind.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Ay, and you had any eye behind you, you might see more detraction at

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: your heels than fortunes before you.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘M.O.A.I.’ This simulation is not as the former: and yet, to crush this

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: a little, it would bow to me, for every one of these letters are in my

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: name. Soft, here follows prose.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: _If this fall into thy hand, revolve. In my stars I am above

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thee, but be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em. Thy fates open

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: their hands, let thy blood and spirit embrace them. And, to inure

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thyself to what thou art like to be, cast thy humble slough and appear

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: fresh. Be opposite with a kinsman, surly with servants. Let thy tongue

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: tang arguments of state; put thyself into the trick of singularity. She

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thus advises thee that sighs for thee. Remember who commended thy

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: yellow stockings, and wished to see thee ever cross-gartered. I say,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: remember. Go to, thou art made, if thou desir’st to be so. If not, let

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: me see thee a steward still, the fellow of servants, and not worthy to

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: touch Fortune’s fingers. Farewell. She that would alter services with

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thee,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: The Fortunate Unhappy._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Daylight and champian discovers not more! This is open. I will be

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: proud, I will read politic authors, I will baffle Sir Toby, I will wash

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: off gross acquaintance, I will be point-device, the very man. I do not

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: now fool myself, to let imagination jade me; for every reason excites

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: to this, that my lady loves me. She did commend my yellow stockings of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: late, she did praise my leg being cross-gartered, and in this she

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: manifests herself to my love, and with a kind of injunction, drives me

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: to these habits of her liking. I thank my stars, I am happy. I will be

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: strange, stout, in yellow stockings, and cross-gartered, even with the

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: swiftness of putting on. Jove and my stars be praised!—Here is yet a

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: postscript. [_Reads._] _Thou canst not choose but know who I am. If

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thou entertain’st my love, let it appear in thy smiling; thy smiles

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: become thee well. Therefore in my presence still smile, dear my sweet,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I prithee._ Jove, I thank thee. I will smile, I will do everything that

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thou wilt have me.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: I will not give my part of this sport for a pension of thousands to be

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: paid from the Sophy.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I could marry this wench for this device.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: So could I too.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And ask no other dowry with her but such another jest.
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Nor I neither.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Here comes my noble gull-catcher.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Wilt thou set thy foot o’ my neck?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Or o’ mine either?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Shall I play my freedom at tray-trip, and become thy bond-slave?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I’ faith, or I either?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, thou hast put him in such a dream, that when the image of it

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: leaves him he must run mad.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nay, but say true, does it work upon him?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Like aqua-vitae with a midwife.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: If you will then see the fruits of the sport, mark his first approach

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: before my lady: he will come to her in yellow stockings, and ’tis a

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: colour she abhors, and cross-gartered, a fashion she detests; and he

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: will smile upon her, which will now be so unsuitable to her

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: disposition, being addicted to a melancholy as she is, that it cannot

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: but turn him into a notable contempt. If you will see it, follow me.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: To the gates of Tartar, thou most excellent devil of wit!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I’ll make one too.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Viola and Clown with a tabor.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Save thee, friend, and thy music. Dost thou live by thy tabor?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No, sir, I live by the church.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Art thou a churchman?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No such matter, sir. I do live by the church, for I do live at my

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: house, and my house doth stand by the church.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: So thou mayst say the king lies by a beggar, if a beggar dwell near

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: him; or the church stands by thy tabor, if thy tabor stand by the

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: church.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: You have said, sir. To see this age! A sentence is but a chev’ril glove

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: to a good wit. How quickly the wrong side may be turned outward!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Nay, that’s certain; they that dally nicely with words may quickly make

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: them wanton.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would, therefore, my sister had had no name, sir.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Why, man?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Why, sir, her name’s a word; and to dally with that word might make my

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: sister wanton. But indeed, words are very rascals, since bonds

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: disgraced them.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Thy reason, man?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Troth, sir, I can yield you none without words, and words are grown so

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: false, I am loath to prove reason with them.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I warrant thou art a merry fellow, and car’st for nothing.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Not so, sir, I do care for something. But in my conscience, sir, I do

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: not care for you. If that be to care for nothing, sir, I would it would

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: make you invisible.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Art not thou the Lady Olivia’s fool?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No, indeed, sir; the Lady Olivia has no folly. She will keep no fool,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: sir, till she be married, and fools are as like husbands as pilchards

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: are to herrings, the husband’s the bigger. I am indeed not her fool,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: but her corrupter of words.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I saw thee late at the Count Orsino’s.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Foolery, sir, does walk about the orb like the sun; it shines

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: everywhere. I would be sorry, sir, but the fool should be as oft with

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: your master as with my mistress. I think I saw your wisdom there.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Nay, and thou pass upon me, I’ll no more with thee. Hold, there’s

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: expenses for thee.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Now Jove, in his next commodity of hair, send thee a beard!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: By my troth, I’ll tell thee, I am almost sick for one, though I would

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: not have it grow on my chin. Is thy lady within?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Would not a pair of these have bred, sir?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Yes, being kept together, and put to use.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would play Lord Pandarus of Phrygia, sir, to bring a Cressida to this

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Troilus.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I understand you, sir; ’tis well begged.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: The matter, I hope, is not great, sir, begging but a beggar: Cressida

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: was a beggar. My lady is within, sir. I will conster to them whence you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: come; who you are and what you would are out of my welkin. I might say

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: “element”, but the word is overworn.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: This fellow is wise enough to play the fool,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And to do that well, craves a kind of wit:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: He must observe their mood on whom he jests,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The quality of persons, and the time,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And like the haggard, check at every feather

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That comes before his eye. This is a practice

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As full of labour as a wise man’s art:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For folly, that he wisely shows, is fit;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But wise men, folly-fall’n, quite taint their wit.
Enter Sir Toby and Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Save you, gentleman.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And you, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: _Dieu vous garde, monsieur._

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: _Et vous aussi; votre serviteur._

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I hope, sir, you are, and I am yours.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Will you encounter the house? My niece is desirous you should enter, if

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: your trade be to her.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am bound to your niece, sir, I mean, she is the list of my voyage.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Taste your legs, sir, put them to motion.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My legs do better understand me, sir, than I understand what you mean

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: by bidding me taste my legs.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I mean, to go, sir, to enter.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I will answer you with gait and entrance: but we are prevented.
Enter Olivia and Maria.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Most excellent accomplished lady, the heavens rain odours on you!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: That youth’s a rare courtier. ‘Rain odours,’ well.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My matter hath no voice, lady, but to your own most pregnant and

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: vouchsafed ear.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ‘Odours,’ ‘pregnant,’ and ‘vouchsafed.’—I’ll get ’em all three ready.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Let the garden door be shut, and leave me to my hearing.
[_Exeunt Sir Toby, Sir Andrew and Maria._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Give me your hand, sir.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My duty, madam, and most humble service.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What is your name?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Cesario is your servant’s name, fair princess.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: My servant, sir! ’Twas never merry world,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Since lowly feigning was call’d compliment:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Y’are servant to the Count Orsino, youth.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And he is yours, and his must needs be yours.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Your servant’s servant is your servant, madam.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: For him, I think not on him: for his thoughts,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Would they were blanks rather than fill’d with me!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Madam, I come to whet your gentle thoughts

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: On his behalf.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, by your leave, I pray you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I bade you never speak again of him.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: But would you undertake another suit,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I had rather hear you to solicit that

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Than music from the spheres.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Dear lady—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Give me leave, beseech you. I did send,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: After the last enchantment you did here,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A ring in chase of you. So did I abuse

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Myself, my servant, and, I fear me, you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Under your hard construction must I sit;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To force that on you in a shameful cunning,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Which you knew none of yours. What might you think?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Have you not set mine honour at the stake,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And baited it with all th’ unmuzzled thoughts

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That tyrannous heart can think? To one of your receiving

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Enough is shown. A cypress, not a bosom,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Hides my heart: so let me hear you speak.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I pity you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That’s a degree to love.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: No, not a grize; for ’tis a vulgar proof

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That very oft we pity enemies.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Why then methinks ’tis time to smile again.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O world, how apt the poor are to be proud!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If one should be a prey, how much the better

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To fall before the lion than the wolf!
[_Clock strikes._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: The clock upbraids me with the waste of time.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Be not afraid, good youth, I will not have you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And yet, when wit and youth is come to harvest,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Your wife is like to reap a proper man.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: There lies your way, due west.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Then westward ho!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Grace and good disposition attend your ladyship!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You’ll nothing, madam, to my lord by me?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Stay:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I prithee tell me what thou think’st of me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That you do think you are not what you are.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If I think so, I think the same of you.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Then think you right; I am not what I am.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I would you were as I would have you be.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Would it be better, madam, than I am?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I wish it might, for now I am your fool.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O what a deal of scorn looks beautiful

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: In the contempt and anger of his lip!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A murd’rous guilt shows not itself more soon

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Than love that would seem hid. Love’s night is noon.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Cesario, by the roses of the spring,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: By maidhood, honour, truth, and everything,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I love thee so, that maugre all thy pride,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Nor wit nor reason can my passion hide.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Do not extort thy reasons from this clause,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: For that I woo, thou therefore hast no cause;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: But rather reason thus with reason fetter:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Love sought is good, but given unsought is better.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: By innocence I swear, and by my youth,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I have one heart, one bosom, and one truth,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And that no woman has; nor never none

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Shall mistress be of it, save I alone.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And so adieu, good madam; never more

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Will I my master’s tears to you deplore.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Yet come again: for thou perhaps mayst move

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That heart, which now abhors, to like his love.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Toby, Sir Andrew and Fabian.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: No, faith, I’ll not stay a jot longer.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Thy reason, dear venom, give thy reason.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: You must needs yield your reason, Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Marry, I saw your niece do more favours to the Count’s servingman than

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ever she bestowed upon me; I saw’t i’ th’ orchard.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Did she see thee the while, old boy? Tell me that.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: As plain as I see you now.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: This was a great argument of love in her toward you.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Slight! will you make an ass o’ me?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: I will prove it legitimate, sir, upon the oaths of judgment and reason.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And they have been grand-jurymen since before Noah was a sailor.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: She did show favour to the youth in your sight only to exasperate you,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: to awake your dormouse valour, to put fire in your heart and brimstone

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: in your liver. You should then have accosted her, and with some

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: excellent jests, fire-new from the mint, you should have banged the

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: youth into dumbness. This was looked for at your hand, and this was

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: balked: the double gilt of this opportunity you let time wash off, and

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: you are now sailed into the north of my lady’s opinion; where you will

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: hang like an icicle on Dutchman’s beard, unless you do redeem it by

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: some laudable attempt, either of valour or policy.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And’t be any way, it must be with valour, for policy I hate; I had as

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: lief be a Brownist as a politician.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, then, build me thy fortunes upon the basis of valour. Challenge me

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: the Count’s youth to fight with him. Hurt him in eleven places; my

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: niece shall take note of it, and assure thyself there is no love-broker

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: in the world can more prevail in man’s commendation with woman than

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: report of valour.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: There is no way but this, Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Will either of you bear me a challenge to him?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Go, write it in a martial hand, be curst and brief; it is no matter how

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: witty, so it be eloquent and full of invention. Taunt him with the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: licence of ink. If thou ‘thou’st’ him some thrice, it shall not be

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: amiss, and as many lies as will lie in thy sheet of paper, although the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: sheet were big enough for the bed of Ware in England, set ’em down. Go

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: about it. Let there be gall enough in thy ink, though thou write with a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: goose-pen, no matter. About it.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Where shall I find you?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: We’ll call thee at the cubiculo. Go.
[_Exit Sir Andrew._]

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: This is a dear manikin to you, Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I have been dear to him, lad, some two thousand strong, or so.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: We shall have a rare letter from him; but you’ll not deliver it.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Never trust me then. And by all means stir on the youth to an answer. I

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: think oxen and wainropes cannot hale them together. For Andrew, if he

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: were opened and you find so much blood in his liver as will clog the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: foot of a flea, I’ll eat the rest of th’ anatomy.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: And his opposite, the youth, bears in his visage no great presage of

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: cruelty.
Enter Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Look where the youngest wren of nine comes.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: If you desire the spleen, and will laugh yourselves into stitches,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: follow me. Yond gull Malvolio is turned heathen, a very renegado; for

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: there is no Christian that means to be saved by believing rightly can

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: ever believe such impossible passages of grossness. He’s in yellow

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: stockings.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: And cross-gartered?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Most villainously; like a pedant that keeps a school i’ th’ church. I

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: have dogged him like his murderer. He does obey every point of the

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: letter that I dropped to betray him. He does smile his face into more

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: lines than is in the new map with the augmentation of the Indies. You

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: have not seen such a thing as ’tis. I  can hardly forbear hurling

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: things at him. I know my lady will strike him. If she do, he’ll smile

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: and take’t for a great favour.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, bring us, bring us where he is.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sebastian and Antonio.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I would not by my will have troubled you,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: But since you make your pleasure of your pains,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I will no further chide you.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I could not stay behind you: my desire,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: More sharp than filed steel, did spur me forth;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And not all love to see you, though so much,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: As might have drawn one to a longer voyage,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But jealousy what might befall your travel,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Being skilless in these parts; which to a stranger,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Unguided and unfriended, often prove

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Rough and unhospitable. My willing love,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: The rather by these arguments of fear,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Set forth in your pursuit.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: My kind Antonio,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I can no other answer make but thanks,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And thanks, and ever thanks; and oft good turns

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Are shuffled off with such uncurrent pay.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: But were my worth, as is my conscience, firm,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: You should find better dealing. What’s to do?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Shall we go see the relics of this town?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Tomorrow, sir; best first go see your lodging.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I am not weary, and ’tis long to night;

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I pray you, let us satisfy our eyes

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: With the memorials and the things of fame

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That do renown this city.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Would you’d pardon me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I do not without danger walk these streets.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Once in a sea-fight, ’gainst the Count his galleys,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I did some service, of such note indeed,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That were I ta’en here, it would scarce be answer’d.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Belike you slew great number of his people.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Th’ offence is not of such a bloody nature,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Albeit the quality of the time and quarrel

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Might well have given us bloody argument.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: It might have since been answered in repaying

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: What we took from them, which for traffic’s sake,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Most of our city did. Only myself stood out,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: For which, if I be lapsed in this place,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I shall pay dear.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Do not then walk too open.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: It doth not fit me. Hold, sir, here’s my purse.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: In the south suburbs, at the Elephant,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Is best to lodge. I will bespeak our diet

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Whiles you beguile the time and feed your knowledge

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: With viewing of the town. There shall you have me.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Why I your purse?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Haply your eye shall light upon some toy

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: You have desire to purchase; and your store,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I think, is not for idle markets, sir.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I’ll be your purse-bearer, and leave you for an hour.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To th’ Elephant.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I do remember.
