Enter Olivia and Maria.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I have sent after him. He says he’ll come;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How shall I feast him? What bestow of him?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: For youth is bought more oft than begg’d or borrow’d.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I speak too loud.—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Where’s Malvolio?—He is sad and civil,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And suits well for a servant with my fortunes;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Where is Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: He’s coming, madam:

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: But in very strange manner. He is sure possessed, madam.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Why, what’s the matter? Does he rave?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: No, madam, he does nothing but smile: your ladyship were best to have

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: some guard about you if he come, for sure the man is tainted in ’s

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: wits.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Go call him hither. I’m as mad as he,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If sad and merry madness equal be.
Enter Malvolio.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How now, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sweet lady, ho, ho!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Smil’st thou? I sent for thee upon a sad occasion.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sad, lady? I could be sad: this does make some obstruction in the

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: blood, this cross-gartering. But what of that? If it please the eye of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: one, it is with me as the very true sonnet is: ‘Please one and please

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: all.’

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Why, how dost thou, man? What is the matter with thee?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Not black in my mind, though yellow in my legs. It did come to his

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: hands, and commands shall be executed. I think we do know the sweet

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Roman hand.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Wilt thou go to bed, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: To bed? Ay, sweetheart, and I’ll come to thee.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: God comfort thee! Why dost thou smile so, and kiss thy hand so oft?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: How do you, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: At your request? Yes, nightingales answer daws!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Why appear you with this ridiculous boldness before my lady?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Be not afraid of greatness.’ ’Twas well writ.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What mean’st thou by that, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Some are born great’—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Ha?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Some achieve greatness’—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What say’st thou?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘And some have greatness thrust upon them.’

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Heaven restore thee!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Remember who commended thy yellow stockings’—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Thy yellow stockings?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘And wished to see thee cross-gartered.’

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Cross-gartered?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Go to: thou art made, if thou desir’st to be so:’—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Am I made?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘If not, let me see thee a servant still.’

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Why, this is very midsummer madness.
Enter Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Madam, the young gentleman of the Count Orsino’s is returned; I could

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: hardly entreat him back. He attends your ladyship’s pleasure.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I’ll come to him.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Good Maria, let this fellow be looked to. Where’s my cousin Toby? Let

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: some of my people have a special care of him; I would not have him

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: miscarry for the half of my dowry.
[_Exeunt Olivia and Maria._]

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: O ho, do you come near me now? No worse man than Sir Toby to look to

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: me. This concurs directly with the letter: she sends him on purpose,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: that I may appear stubborn to him; for she incites me to that in the

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: letter. ‘Cast thy humble slough,’ says she; ‘be opposite with a

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: kinsman, surly with servants, let thy tongue tang with arguments of

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: state, put thyself into the trick of singularity,’ and consequently,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: sets down the manner how: as, a sad face, a reverend carriage, a slow

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: tongue, in the habit of some sir of note, and so forth. I have limed

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: her, but it is Jove’s doing, and Jove make me thankful! And when she

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: went away now, ‘Let this fellow be looked to;’ ‘Fellow!’ not

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: ‘Malvolio’, nor after my degree, but ‘fellow’. Why, everything adheres

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: together, that no dram of a scruple, no scruple of a scruple, no

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: obstacle, no incredulous or unsafe circumstance. What can be said?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Nothing that can be can come between me and the full prospect of my

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: hopes. Well, Jove, not I, is the doer of this, and he is to be thanked.
Enter Sir Toby, Fabian and Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Which way is he, in the name of sanctity? If all the devils of hell be

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: drawn in little, and Legion himself possessed him, yet I’ll speak to

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Here he is, here he is. How is’t with you, sir? How is’t with you, man?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Go off, I discard you. Let me enjoy my private. Go off.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Lo, how hollow the fiend speaks within him! Did not I tell you? Sir

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Toby, my lady prays you to have a care of him.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Ah, ha! does she so?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Go to, go to; peace, peace, we must deal gently with him. Let me alone.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: How do you, Malvolio? How is’t with you? What, man! defy the devil!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Consider, he’s an enemy to mankind.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Do you know what you say?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: La you, an you speak ill of the devil, how he takes it at heart! Pray

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: God he be not bewitched.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Carry his water to th’ wise woman.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Marry, and it shall be done tomorrow morning, if I live. My lady would

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: not lose him for more than I’ll say.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: How now, mistress!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: O Lord!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Prithee hold thy peace, this is not the way. Do you not see you move

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: him? Let me alone with him.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: No way but gentleness, gently, gently. The fiend is rough, and will not

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: be roughly used.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, how now, my bawcock? How dost thou, chuck?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Ay, biddy, come with me. What, man, ’tis not for gravity to play at

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: cherry-pit with Satan. Hang him, foul collier!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Get him to say his prayers, good Sir Toby, get him to pray.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: My prayers, minx?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: No, I warrant you, he will not hear of godliness.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Go, hang yourselves all! You are idle, shallow things. I am not of your

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: element. You shall know more hereafter.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: If this were played upon a stage now, I could condemn it as an

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: improbable fiction.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: His very genius hath taken the infection of the device, man.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nay, pursue him now, lest the device take air and taint.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Why, we shall make him mad indeed.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: The house will be the quieter.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, we’ll have him in a dark room and bound. My niece is already in

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: the belief that he’s mad. We may carry it thus for our pleasure, and

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: his penance, till our very pastime, tired out of breath, prompt us to

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: have mercy on him, at which time we will bring the device to the bar,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: and crown thee for a finder of madmen. But see, but see!
Enter Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: More matter for a May morning.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Here’s the challenge, read it. I warrant there’s vinegar and pepper

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: in’t.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Is’t so saucy?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Ay, is’t, I warrant him. Do but read.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Give me. [_Reads._] _Youth, whatsoever thou art, thou art but a scurvy

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: fellow._

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Good, and valiant.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Wonder not, nor admire not in thy mind, why I do call thee so, for I

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: will show thee no reason for’t._

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: A good note, that keeps you from the blow of the law.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Thou comest to the Lady Olivia, and in my sight she uses thee kindly:

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: but thou liest in thy throat; that is not the matter I challenge thee

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: for._

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Very brief, and to exceeding good sense—less.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _I will waylay thee going home; where if it be thy chance to kill me—_

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Thou kill’st me like a rogue and a villain._

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Still you keep o’ th’ windy side of the law. Good.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: _Fare thee well, and God have mercy upon one of our souls! He may have

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: mercy upon mine, but my hope is better, and so look to thyself. Thy

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: friend, as thou usest him, and thy sworn enemy,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Andrew Aguecheek._

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: If this letter move him not, his legs cannot. I’ll give’t him.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: You may have very fit occasion for’t. He is now in some commerce with

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: my lady, and will by and by depart.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Go, Sir Andrew. Scout me for him at the corner of the orchard, like a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: bum-baily. So soon as ever thou seest him, draw, and as thou draw’st,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: swear horrible, for it comes to pass oft that a terrible oath, with a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: swaggering accent sharply twanged off, gives manhood more approbation

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: than ever proof itself would have earned him. Away.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Nay, let me alone for swearing.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Now will not I deliver his letter, for the behaviour of the young

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: gentleman gives him out to be of good capacity and breeding; his

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: employment between his lord and my niece confirms no less. Therefore

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: this letter, being so excellently ignorant, will breed no terror in the

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: youth. He will find it comes from a clodpole. But, sir, I will deliver

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: his challenge by word of mouth, set upon Aguecheek notable report of

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: valour, and drive the gentleman (as I know his youth will aptly receive

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: it) into a most hideous opinion of his rage, skill, fury, and

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: impetuosity. This will so fright them both that they will kill one

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: another by the look, like cockatrices.
Enter Olivia and Viola.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Here he comes with your niece; give them way till he take leave, and

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: presently after him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I will meditate the while upon some horrid message for a challenge.
[_Exeunt Sir Toby, Fabian and Maria._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I have said too much unto a heart of stone,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And laid mine honour too unchary on’t:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: There’s something in me that reproves my fault:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: But such a headstrong potent fault it is,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That it but mocks reproof.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: With the same ’haviour that your passion bears

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Goes on my master’s griefs.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Here, wear this jewel for me, ’tis my picture.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Refuse it not, it hath no tongue to vex you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And I beseech you come again tomorrow.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What shall you ask of me that I’ll deny,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That honour sav’d, may upon asking give?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Nothing but this, your true love for my master.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How with mine honour may I give him that

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Which I have given to you?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I will acquit you.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Well, come again tomorrow. Fare thee well;

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A fiend like thee might bear my soul to hell.
[_Exit._]
Enter Sir Toby and Fabian.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Gentleman, God save thee.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And you, sir.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: That defence thou hast, betake thee to’t. Of what nature the wrongs are

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: thou hast done him, I know not, but thy intercepter, full of despite,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: bloody as the hunter, attends thee at the orchard end. Dismount thy

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: tuck, be yare in thy preparation, for thy assailant is quick, skilful,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: and deadly.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You mistake, sir; I am sure no man hath any quarrel to me. My

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: remembrance is very free and clear from any image of offence done to

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: any man.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: You’ll find it otherwise, I assure you. Therefore, if you hold your

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: life at any price, betake you to your guard, for your opposite hath in

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: him what youth, strength, skill, and wrath, can furnish man withal.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I pray you, sir, what is he?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: He is knight, dubbed with unhatched rapier, and on carpet

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: consideration, but he is a devil in private brawl. Souls and bodies

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: hath he divorced three, and his incensement at this moment is so

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: implacable that satisfaction can be none but by pangs of death and

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: sepulchre. Hob, nob is his word; give’t or take’t.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I will return again into the house and desire some conduct of the lady.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I am no fighter. I have heard of some kind of men that put quarrels

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: purposely on others to taste their valour: belike this is a man of that

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: quirk.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Sir, no. His indignation derives itself out of a very competent injury;

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: therefore, get you on and give him his desire. Back you shall not to

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: the house, unless you undertake that with me which with as much safety

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: you might answer him. Therefore on, or strip your sword stark naked,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: for meddle you must, that’s certain, or forswear to wear iron about

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: you.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: This is as uncivil as strange. I beseech you, do me this courteous

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: office, as to know of the knight what my offence to him is. It is

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: something of my negligence, nothing of my purpose.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I will do so. Signior Fabian, stay you by this gentleman till my

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: return.
[_Exit Sir Toby._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Pray you, sir, do you know of this matter?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: I know the knight is incensed against you, even to a mortal

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: arbitrement, but nothing of the circumstance more.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I beseech you, what manner of man is he?

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Nothing of that wonderful promise, to read him by his form, as you are

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: like to find him in the proof of his valour. He is indeed, sir, the

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: most skilful, bloody, and fatal opposite that you could possibly have

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: found in any part of Illyria. Will you walk towards him? I will make

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: your peace with him if I can.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I shall be much bound to you for’t. I am one that had rather go with

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: sir priest than sir knight: I care not who knows so much of my mettle.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Toby and Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Why, man, he’s a very devil. I have not seen such a firago. I had a

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: pass with him, rapier, scabbard, and all, and he gives me the stuck-in

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: with such a mortal motion that it is inevitable; and on the answer, he

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: pays you as surely as your feet hits the ground they step on. They say

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: he has been fencer to the Sophy.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Pox on’t, I’ll not meddle with him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Ay, but he will not now be pacified: Fabian can scarce hold him yonder.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Plague on’t, an I thought he had been valiant, and so cunning in fence,

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I’d have seen him damned ere I’d have challenged him. Let him let the

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: matter slip, and I’ll give him my horse, grey Capilet.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I’ll make the motion. Stand here, make a good show on’t. This shall end

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: without the perdition of souls. [_Aside._] Marry, I’ll ride your horse

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: as well as I ride you.
Enter Fabian and Viola.
[_To Fabian._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I have his horse to take up the quarrel. I have

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: persuaded him the youth’s a devil.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: He is as horribly conceited of him, and pants and looks pale, as if a

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: bear were at his heels.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: There’s no remedy, sir, he will fight with you for’s oath sake. Marry,

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: he hath better bethought him of his quarrel, and he finds that now

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: scarce to be worth talking of. Therefore, draw for the supportance of

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: his vow; he protests he will not hurt you.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Pray God defend me! A little thing would make me tell them

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: how much I lack of a man.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Give ground if you see him furious.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, Sir Andrew, there’s no remedy, the gentleman will for his

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: honour’s sake have one bout with you. He cannot by the duello avoid it;

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: but he has promised me, as he is a gentleman and a soldier, he will not

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: hurt you. Come on: to’t.
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Pray God he keep his oath!
Enter Antonio.
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I do assure you ’tis against my will.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Put up your sword. If this young gentleman

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Have done offence, I take the fault on me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: If you offend him, I for him defy you.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: You, sir? Why, what are you?
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: One, sir, that for his love dares yet do more

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Than you have heard him brag to you he will.
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Nay, if you be an undertaker, I am for you.
Enter Officers.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: O good Sir Toby, hold! Here come the officers.
[_To Antonio._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I’ll be with you anon.
[_To Sir Andrew._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Pray, sir, put your sword up, if you please.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Marry, will I, sir; and for that I promised you, I’ll be as good as my

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: word. He will bear you easily, and reins well.

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: This is the man; do thy office.

lines.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
lines.text: Antonio, I arrest thee at the suit

lines.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
lines.text: Of Count Orsino.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: You do mistake me, sir.

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: No, sir, no jot. I know your favour well,

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: Though now you have no sea-cap on your head.—

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: Take him away, he knows I know him well.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I must obey. This comes with seeking you;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But there’s no remedy, I shall answer it.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: What will you do? Now my necessity

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Makes me to ask you for my purse. It grieves me

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Much more for what I cannot do for you,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Than what befalls myself. You stand amaz’d,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But be of comfort.

lines.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
lines.text: Come, sir, away.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I must entreat of you some of that money.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: What money, sir?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For the fair kindness you have show’d me here,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And part being prompted by your present trouble,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Out of my lean and low ability

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I’ll lend you something. My having is not much;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I’ll make division of my present with you.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Hold, there’s half my coffer.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Will you deny me now?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Is’t possible that my deserts to you

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Can lack persuasion? Do not tempt my misery,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Lest that it make me so unsound a man

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: As to upbraid you with those kindnesses

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That I have done for you.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I know of none,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Nor know I you by voice or any feature.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I hate ingratitude more in a man

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Than lying, vainness, babbling, drunkenness,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Or any taint of vice whose strong corruption

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Inhabits our frail blood.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: O heavens themselves!

lines.speaker: SECOND OFFICER
lines.text: Come, sir, I pray you go.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Let me speak a little. This youth that you see here

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I snatch’d one half out of the jaws of death,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Reliev’d him with such sanctity of love;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And to his image, which methought did promise

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Most venerable worth, did I devotion.

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: What’s that to us? The time goes by. Away!

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But O how vile an idol proves this god!

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Thou hast, Sebastian, done good feature shame.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: In nature there’s no blemish but the mind;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: None can be call’d deform’d but the unkind.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Virtue is beauty, but the beauteous evil

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Are empty trunks, o’erflourished by the devil.

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: The man grows mad, away with him. Come, come, sir.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Lead me on.
[_Exeunt Officers with Antonio._]

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Methinks his words do from such passion fly

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That he believes himself; so do not I.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Prove true, imagination, O prove true,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That I, dear brother, be now ta’en for you!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come hither, knight; come hither, Fabian. We’ll whisper o’er a couplet

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: or two of most sage saws.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: He nam’d Sebastian. I my brother know

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Yet living in my glass; even such and so

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: In favour was my brother, and he went

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Still in this fashion, colour, ornament,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: For him I imitate. O if it prove,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Tempests are kind, and salt waves fresh in love!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: A very dishonest paltry boy, and more a coward than a hare. His

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: dishonesty appears in leaving his friend here in necessity, and denying

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: him; and for his cowardship, ask Fabian.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: A coward, a most devout coward, religious in it.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Slid, I’ll after him again and beat him.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Do, cuff him soundly, but never draw thy sword.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: And I do not—
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Come, let’s see the event.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: I dare lay any money ’twill be nothing yet.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sebastian and Clown.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Will you make me believe that I am not sent for you?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Go to, go to, thou art a foolish fellow.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Let me be clear of thee.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Well held out, i’ faith! No, I do not know you, nor I am not sent to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you by my lady, to bid you come speak with her; nor your name is not

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Master Cesario; nor this is not my nose neither. Nothing that is so, is

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: so.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I prithee vent thy folly somewhere else,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Thou know’st not me.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Vent my folly! He has heard that word of some great man, and now

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: applies it to a fool. Vent my folly! I am afraid this great lubber, the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: world, will prove a cockney. I prithee now, ungird thy strangeness, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: tell me what I shall vent to my lady. Shall I vent to her that thou art

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: coming?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I prithee, foolish Greek, depart from me.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: There’s money for thee; if you tarry longer

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I shall give worse payment.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: By my troth, thou hast an open hand. These wise men that give fools

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: money get themselves a good report—after fourteen years’ purchase.
Enter Sir Andrew, Sir Toby and Fabian.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Now sir, have I met you again? There’s for you.
[_Striking Sebastian._]

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Why, there’s for thee, and there, and there.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Are all the people mad?
[_Beating Sir Andrew._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Hold, sir, or I’ll throw your dagger o’er the house.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: This will I tell my lady straight. I would not be in some of your coats

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: for twopence.
[_Exit Clown._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come on, sir, hold!

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: Nay, let him alone, I’ll go another way to work with him. I’ll have an

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: action of battery against him, if there be any law in Illyria. Though I

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: struck him first, yet it’s no matter for that.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Let go thy hand!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come, sir, I will not let you go. Come, my young soldier, put up your

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: iron: you are well fleshed. Come on.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I will be free from thee. What wouldst thou now?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: If thou dar’st tempt me further, draw thy sword.
[_Draws._]

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: What, what? Nay, then, I must have an ounce or two of this malapert

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: blood from you.
[_Draws._]
Enter Olivia.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Hold, Toby! On thy life I charge thee hold!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Madam.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Will it be ever thus? Ungracious wretch,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Fit for the mountains and the barbarous caves,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Where manners ne’er were preach’d! Out of my sight!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Be not offended, dear Cesario.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Rudesby, be gone!
[_Exeunt Sir Toby, Sir Andrew and Fabian._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: I prithee, gentle friend,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Let thy fair wisdom, not thy passion, sway

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: In this uncivil and unjust extent

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Against thy peace. Go with me to my house,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And hear thou there how many fruitless pranks

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: This ruffian hath botch’d up, that thou thereby

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Mayst smile at this. Thou shalt not choose but go.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Do not deny. Beshrew his soul for me,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: He started one poor heart of mine, in thee.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: What relish is in this? How runs the stream?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Or I am mad, or else this is a dream.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Let fancy still my sense in Lethe steep;

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: If it be thus to dream, still let me sleep!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Nay, come, I prithee. Would thou’dst be ruled by me!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Madam, I will.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, say so, and so be!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Maria and Clown.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nay, I prithee, put on this gown and this beard; make him believe thou

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: art Sir Topas the curate. Do it quickly. I’ll call Sir Toby the whilst.
[_Exit Maria._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Well, I’ll put it on, and I will dissemble myself in’t, and I would I

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: were the first that ever dissembled in such a gown. I am not tall

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: enough to become the function well, nor lean enough to be thought a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: good student, but to be said, an honest man and a good housekeeper goes

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: as fairly as to say, a careful man and a great scholar. The competitors

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: enter.
Enter Sir Toby and Maria.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Jove bless thee, Master Parson.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _Bonos dies_, Sir Toby: for as the old hermit of Prague, that never saw

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: pen and ink, very wittily said to a niece of King Gorboduc, ‘That that

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: is, is’: so I, being Master Parson, am Master Parson; for what is

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: ‘that’ but ‘that’? and ‘is’ but ‘is’?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: To him, Sir Topas.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What ho, I say! Peace in this prison!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: The knave counterfeits well. A good knave.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Malvolio within.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Who calls there?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Sir Topas the curate, who comes to visit Malvolio the lunatic.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas, good Sir Topas, go to my lady.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Out, hyperbolical fiend! how vexest thou this man? Talkest thou nothing

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: but of ladies?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Well said, Master Parson.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir Topas, never was man thus wronged. Good Sir Topas, do not think I

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: am mad. They have laid me here in hideous darkness.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Fie, thou dishonest Satan! I call thee by the most modest terms, for I

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: am one of those gentle ones that will use the devil himself with

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: courtesy. Say’st thou that house is dark?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: As hell, Sir Topas.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Why, it hath bay windows transparent as barricadoes, and the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: clerestories toward the south-north are as lustrous as ebony; and yet

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: complainest thou of obstruction?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I am not mad, Sir Topas. I say to you this house is dark.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Madman, thou errest. I say there is no darkness but ignorance, in which

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I say this house is as dark as ignorance, though ignorance were as dark

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: as hell; and I say there was never man thus abused. I am no more mad

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: than you are. Make the trial of it in any constant question.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What is the opinion of Pythagoras concerning wildfowl?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: That the soul of our grandam might haply inhabit a bird.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What think’st thou of his opinion?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I think nobly of the soul, and no way approve his opinion.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Fare thee well. Remain thou still in darkness. Thou shalt hold the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: opinion of Pythagoras ere I will allow of thy wits, and fear to kill a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: woodcock, lest thou dispossess the soul of thy grandam. Fare thee well.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir Topas, Sir Topas!

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: My most exquisite Sir Topas!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Nay, I am for all waters.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Thou mightst have done this without thy beard and gown. He sees thee

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: not.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: To him in thine own voice, and bring me word how thou find’st him. I

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: would we were well rid of this knavery. If he may be conveniently

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: delivered, I would he were, for I am now so far in offence with my

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: niece that I cannot pursue with any safety this sport to the upshot.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Come by and by to my chamber.
[_Exeunt Sir Toby and Maria._]
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _Hey, Robin, jolly Robin,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Tell me how thy lady does._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _My lady is unkind, perdy._

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _Alas, why is she so?_

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool, I say!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _She loves another_—

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Who calls, ha?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Good fool, as ever thou wilt deserve well at my hand, help me to a

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: candle, and pen, ink, and paper. As I am a gentleman, I will live to be

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: thankful to thee for’t.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Master Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Ay, good fool.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alas, sir, how fell you besides your five wits?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool, there was never man so notoriously abused. I am as well in my

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: wits, fool, as thou art.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: But as well? Then you are mad indeed, if you be no better in your wits

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: than a fool.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: They have here propertied me; keep me in darkness, send ministers to

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: me, asses, and do all they can to face me out of my wits.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Advise you what you say: the minister is here.
[_As Sir Topas_]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Malvolio, Malvolio, thy wits the heavens restore. Endeavour thyself to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: sleep, and leave thy vain bibble-babble.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Sir Topas!
[_As Sir Topas_]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Maintain no words with him, good fellow. [_As

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: himself_] Who, I, sir? not I, sir. God buy you, good Sir Topas. [_As

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Sir Topas_] Marry, amen. [_As himself_] I will sir, I will.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool, fool, fool, I say!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alas, sir, be patient. What say you, sir? I am shent for speaking to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Good fool, help me to some light and some paper. I tell thee I am as

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: well in my wits as any man in Illyria.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Well-a-day that you were, sir!

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: By this hand, I am. Good fool, some ink, paper, and light, and convey

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: what I will set down to my lady. It shall advantage thee more than ever

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: the bearing of letter did.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I will help you to’t. But tell me true, are you not mad indeed? or do

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you but counterfeit?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Believe me, I am not. I tell thee true.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Nay, I’ll ne’er believe a madman till I see his brains. I will fetch

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you light, and paper, and ink.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Fool, I’ll requite it in the highest degree: I prithee be gone.
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _I am gone, sir, and anon, sir,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I’ll be with you again,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: In a trice, like to the old Vice,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Your need to sustain;

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Who with dagger of lath, in his rage and his wrath,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Cries ‘ah, ha!’ to the devil:

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Like a mad lad, ‘Pare thy nails, dad.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Adieu, goodman devil.’_
[_Exit._]
Enter Sebastian.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: This is the air; that is the glorious sun,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: This pearl she gave me, I do feel’t and see’t,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And though ’tis wonder that enwraps me thus,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Yet ’tis not madness. Where’s Antonio, then?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I could not find him at the Elephant,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Yet there he was, and there I found this credit,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That he did range the town to seek me out.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: His counsel now might do me golden service.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: For though my soul disputes well with my sense

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That this may be some error, but no madness,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Yet doth this accident and flood of fortune

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: So far exceed all instance, all discourse,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That I am ready to distrust mine eyes

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And wrangle with my reason that persuades me

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: To any other trust but that I am mad,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Or else the lady’s mad; yet if ’twere so,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: She could not sway her house, command her followers,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Take and give back affairs and their dispatch,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: With such a smooth, discreet, and stable bearing

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: As I perceive she does. There’s something in’t

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That is deceivable. But here the lady comes.
Enter Olivia and a Priest.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Blame not this haste of mine. If you mean well,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Now go with me and with this holy man

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Into the chantry by: there, before him

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And underneath that consecrated roof,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Plight me the full assurance of your faith,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That my most jealous and too doubtful soul

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: May live at peace. He shall conceal it

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Whiles you are willing it shall come to note,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What time we will our celebration keep

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: According to my birth. What do you say?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I’ll follow this good man, and go with you,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And having sworn truth, ever will be true.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Then lead the way, good father, and heavens so shine,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That they may fairly note this act of mine!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Clown and Fabian.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Now, as thou lov’st me, let me see his letter.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Good Master Fabian, grant me another request.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Anything.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Do not desire to see this letter.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: This is to give a dog, and in recompense desire my dog again.
Enter Duke, Viola, Curio and Lords.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Belong you to the Lady Olivia, friends?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, sir, we are some of her trappings.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I know thee well. How dost thou, my good fellow?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Truly, sir, the better for my foes, and the worse for my friends.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Just the contrary; the better for thy friends.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No, sir, the worse.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How can that be?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Marry, sir, they praise me, and make an ass of me. Now my foes tell me

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: plainly I am an ass: so that by my foes, sir, I profit in the knowledge

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: of myself, and by my friends I am abused. So that, conclusions to be as

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: kisses, if your four negatives make your two affirmatives, why then,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the worse for my friends, and the better for my foes.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why, this is excellent.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: By my troth, sir, no; though it please you to be one of my friends.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou shalt not be the worse for me; there’s gold.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: But that it would be double-dealing, sir, I would you could make it

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: another.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, you give me ill counsel.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Put your grace in your pocket, sir, for this once, and let your flesh

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: and blood obey it.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Well, I will be so much a sinner to be a double-dealer: there’s

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: another.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: _Primo, secundo, tertio_, is a good play, and the old saying is, the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: third pays for all; the triplex, sir, is a good tripping measure; or

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the bells of Saint Bennet, sir, may put you in mind—one, two, three.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: You can fool no more money out of me at this throw. If you will let

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: your lady know I am here to speak with her, and bring her along with

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: you, it may awake my bounty further.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Marry, sir, lullaby to your bounty till I come again. I go, sir, but I

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: would not have you to think that my desire of having is the sin of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: covetousness: but as you say, sir, let your bounty take a nap, I will

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: awake it anon.
[_Exit Clown._]
Enter Antonio and Officers.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Here comes the man, sir, that did rescue me.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That face of his I do remember well.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Yet when I saw it last it was besmear’d

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: As black as Vulcan, in the smoke of war.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A baubling vessel was he captain of,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For shallow draught and bulk unprizable,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With which such scathful grapple did he make

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With the most noble bottom of our fleet,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That very envy and the tongue of loss

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Cried fame and honour on him. What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: Orsino, this is that Antonio

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: That took the _Phoenix_ and her fraught from Candy,

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: And this is he that did the _Tiger_ board

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: When your young nephew Titus lost his leg.

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: Here in the streets, desperate of shame and state,

lines.speaker: FIRST OFFICER
lines.text: In private brabble did we apprehend him.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: He did me kindness, sir; drew on my side,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But in conclusion, put strange speech upon me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I know not what ’twas, but distraction.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Notable pirate, thou salt-water thief,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What foolish boldness brought thee to their mercies,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Whom thou, in terms so bloody and so dear,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hast made thine enemies?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Orsino, noble sir,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Be pleased that I shake off these names you give me:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Antonio never yet was thief or pirate,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Though, I confess, on base and ground enough,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Orsino’s enemy. A witchcraft drew me hither:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That most ingrateful boy there by your side

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: From the rude sea’s enraged and foamy mouth

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Did I redeem; a wreck past hope he was.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: His life I gave him, and did thereto add

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: My love, without retention or restraint,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: All his in dedication. For his sake

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Did I expose myself, pure for his love,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Into the danger of this adverse town;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Drew to defend him when he was beset;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Where being apprehended, his false cunning

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: (Not meaning to partake with me in danger)

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Taught him to face me out of his acquaintance,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And grew a twenty years’ removed thing

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: While one would wink; denied me mine own purse,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Which I had recommended to his use

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Not half an hour before.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: How can this be?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: When came he to this town?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Today, my lord; and for three months before,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: No int’rim, not a minute’s vacancy,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Both day and night did we keep company.
Enter Olivia and Attendants.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Here comes the Countess, now heaven walks on earth.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But for thee, fellow, fellow, thy words are madness.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Three months this youth hath tended upon me;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But more of that anon. Take him aside.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What would my lord, but that he may not have,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Wherein Olivia may seem serviceable?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Cesario, you do not keep promise with me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Madam?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Gracious Olivia—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What do you say, Cesario? Good my lord—

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My lord would speak, my duty hushes me.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: If it be aught to the old tune, my lord,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: It is as fat and fulsome to mine ear

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: As howling after music.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Still so cruel?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Still so constant, lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What, to perverseness? You uncivil lady,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To whose ingrate and unauspicious altars

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My soul the faithfull’st off’rings hath breathed out

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That e’er devotion tender’d! What shall I do?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Even what it please my lord that shall become him.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why should I not, had I the heart to do it,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Like to the Egyptian thief at point of death,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Kill what I love?—a savage jealousy

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That sometime savours nobly. But hear me this:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Since you to non-regardance cast my faith,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And that I partly know the instrument

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That screws me from my true place in your favour,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Live you the marble-breasted tyrant still.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But this your minion, whom I know you love,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And whom, by heaven I swear, I tender dearly,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Him will I tear out of that cruel eye

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Where he sits crowned in his master’s spite.—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Come, boy, with me; my thoughts are ripe in mischief:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I’ll sacrifice the lamb that I do love,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To spite a raven’s heart within a dove.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And I, most jocund, apt, and willingly,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: To do you rest, a thousand deaths would die.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Where goes Cesario?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: After him I love

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: More than I love these eyes, more than my life,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: More, by all mores, than e’er I shall love wife.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If I do feign, you witnesses above

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Punish my life for tainting of my love.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Ah me, detested! how am I beguil’d!

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Who does beguile you? Who does do you wrong?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Hast thou forgot thyself? Is it so long?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Call forth the holy father.
[_Exit an Attendant._]
[_To Viola._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Come, away!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Whither, my lord? Cesario, husband, stay.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Husband?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Ay, husband. Can he that deny?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Her husband, sirrah?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: No, my lord, not I.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Alas, it is the baseness of thy fear

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: That makes thee strangle thy propriety.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Fear not, Cesario, take thy fortunes up.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Be that thou know’st thou art, and then thou art

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: As great as that thou fear’st.
Enter Priest.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, welcome, father!

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Father, I charge thee, by thy reverence

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Here to unfold—though lately we intended

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To keep in darkness what occasion now

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Reveals before ’tis ripe—what thou dost know

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Hath newly passed between this youth and me.

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: A contract of eternal bond of love,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Confirmed by mutual joinder of your hands,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Attested by the holy close of lips,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Strengthen’d by interchangement of your rings,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: And all the ceremony of this compact

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Sealed in my function, by my testimony;

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: Since when, my watch hath told me, toward my grave,

lines.speaker: PRIEST
lines.text: I have travelled but two hours.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O thou dissembling cub! What wilt thou be

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: When time hath sowed a grizzle on thy case?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Or will not else thy craft so quickly grow

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That thine own trip shall be thine overthrow?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Farewell, and take her; but direct thy feet

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Where thou and I henceforth may never meet.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My lord, I do protest—

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: O, do not swear.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Hold little faith, though thou has too much fear.
Enter Sir Andrew.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: For the love of God, a surgeon! Send one presently to Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Has broke my head across, and has given Sir Toby a bloody coxcomb too.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: For the love of God, your help! I had rather than forty pound I were at

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: home.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Who has done this, Sir Andrew?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: The Count’s gentleman, one Cesario. We took him for a coward, but he’s

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: the very devil incardinate.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My gentleman, Cesario?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: ’Od’s lifelings, here he is!—You broke my head for nothing; and that

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: that I did, I was set on to do’t by Sir Toby.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Why do you speak to me? I never hurt you:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You drew your sword upon me without cause,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But I bespake you fair and hurt you not.
Enter Sir Toby, drunk, led by the Clown.

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: If a bloody coxcomb be a hurt, you have hurt me. I think you set

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: nothing by a bloody coxcomb. Here comes Sir Toby halting, you shall

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: hear more: but if he had not been in drink, he would have tickled you

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: othergates than he did.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How now, gentleman? How is’t with you?

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: That’s all one; ’has hurt me, and there’s th’ end on’t. Sot, didst see

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Dick Surgeon, sot?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: O, he’s drunk, Sir Toby, an hour agone; his eyes were set at eight i’

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: th’ morning.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Then he’s a rogue, and a passy measures pavin. I hate a drunken rogue.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Away with him. Who hath made this havoc with them?

lines.speaker: SIR ANDREW
lines.text: I’ll help you, Sir Toby, because we’ll be dressed together.

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: Will you help? An ass-head, and a coxcomb, and a knave, a thin-faced

lines.speaker: SIR TOBY
lines.text: knave, a gull?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Get him to bed, and let his hurt be looked to.
[_Exeunt Clown, Fabian, Sir Toby and Sir Andrew._]
Enter Sebastian.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I am sorry, madam, I have hurt your kinsman;

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: But had it been the brother of my blood,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I must have done no less with wit and safety.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: You throw a strange regard upon me, and by that

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I do perceive it hath offended you.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Pardon me, sweet one, even for the vows

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: We made each other but so late ago.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: One face, one voice, one habit, and two persons!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A natural perspective, that is, and is not!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Antonio, O my dear Antonio!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: How have the hours rack’d and tortur’d me

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Since I have lost thee.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Sebastian are you?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Fear’st thou that, Antonio?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: How have you made division of yourself?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: An apple cleft in two is not more twin

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Than these two creatures. Which is Sebastian?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Most wonderful!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Do I stand there? I never had a brother:

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Nor can there be that deity in my nature

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Of here and everywhere. I had a sister,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Whom the blind waves and surges have devoured.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Of charity, what kin are you to me?

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: What countryman? What name? What parentage?

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Of Messaline: Sebastian was my father;

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Such a Sebastian was my brother too:

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: So went he suited to his watery tomb.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If spirits can assume both form and suit,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: You come to fright us.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: A spirit I am indeed,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: But am in that dimension grossly clad,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Which from the womb I did participate.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Were you a woman, as the rest goes even,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: I should my tears let fall upon your cheek,

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And say, ‘Thrice welcome, drowned Viola.’

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: My father had a mole upon his brow.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: And so had mine.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And died that day when Viola from her birth

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Had numbered thirteen years.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: O, that record is lively in my soul!

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: He finished indeed his mortal act

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: That day that made my sister thirteen years.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: If nothing lets to make us happy both

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: But this my masculine usurp’d attire,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Do not embrace me till each circumstance

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Of place, time, fortune, do cohere and jump

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That I am Viola; which to confirm,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I’ll bring you to a captain in this town,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Where lie my maiden weeds; by whose gentle help

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: I was preserv’d to serve this noble count.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: All the occurrence of my fortune since

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Hath been between this lady and this lord.
[_To Olivia._]

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: So comes it, lady, you have been mistook.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: But nature to her bias drew in that.

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: You would have been contracted to a maid;

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: Nor are you therein, by my life, deceived:

lines.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines.text: You are betroth’d both to a maid and man.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be not amazed; right noble is his blood.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If this be so, as yet the glass seems true,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I shall have share in this most happy wreck.
[_To Viola._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Boy, thou hast said to me a thousand times

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou never shouldst love woman like to me.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And all those sayings will I over-swear,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: And all those swearings keep as true in soul

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: As doth that orbed continent the fire

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: That severs day from night.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Give me thy hand,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And let me see thee in thy woman’s weeds.

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: The captain that did bring me first on shore

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Hath my maid’s garments. He, upon some action,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: Is now in durance, at Malvolio’s suit,

lines.speaker: VIOLA
lines.text: A gentleman and follower of my lady’s.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: He shall enlarge him. Fetch Malvolio hither.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And yet, alas, now I remember me,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: They say, poor gentleman, he’s much distract.
Enter Clown, with a letter and Fabian.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A most extracting frenzy of mine own

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: From my remembrance clearly banished his.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How does he, sirrah?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Truly, madam, he holds Belzebub at the stave’s end as well as a man in

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: his case may do. Has here writ a letter to you. I should have given it

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you today morning, but as a madman’s epistles are no gospels, so it

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: skills not much when they are delivered.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Open ’t, and read it.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Look then to be well edified, when the fool delivers the madman. _By

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the Lord, madam,—_

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How now, art thou mad?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No, madam, I do but read madness: an your ladyship will have it as it

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: ought to be, you must allow _vox_.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Prithee, read i’ thy right wits.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: So I do, madonna. But to read his right wits is to read thus; therefore

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: perpend, my princess, and give ear.
[_To Fabian._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Read it you, sirrah.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: _By the Lord, madam, you wrong me, and the world shall know

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: it. Though you have put me into darkness and given your drunken cousin

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: rule over me, yet have I the benefit of my senses as well as your

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: ladyship. I have your own letter that induced me to the semblance I put

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: on; with the which I doubt not but to do myself much right or you much

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: shame. Think of me as you please. I leave my duty a little unthought

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: of, and speak out of my injury.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: The madly-used Malvolio._

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Did he write this?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, madam.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: This savours not much of distraction.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: See him delivered, Fabian, bring him hither.
[_Exit Fabian._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: My lord, so please you, these things further thought on,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: To think me as well a sister, as a wife,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: One day shall crown th’ alliance on’t, so please you,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Here at my house, and at my proper cost.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Madam, I am most apt t’ embrace your offer.
[_To Viola._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Your master quits you; and for your service done him,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So much against the mettle of your sex,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So far beneath your soft and tender breeding,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And since you call’d me master for so long,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Here is my hand; you shall from this time be

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Your master’s mistress.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: A sister? You are she.
Enter Fabian and Malvolio.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Is this the madman?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Ay, my lord, this same.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: How now, Malvolio?

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Madam, you have done me wrong,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Notorious wrong.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Have I, Malvolio? No.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Lady, you have. Pray you peruse that letter.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: You must not now deny it is your hand,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Write from it, if you can, in hand, or phrase,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Or say ’tis not your seal, not your invention:

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: You can say none of this. Well, grant it then,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: And tell me, in the modesty of honour,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Why you have given me such clear lights of favour,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Bade me come smiling and cross-garter’d to you,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: To put on yellow stockings, and to frown

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Upon Sir Toby, and the lighter people;

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: And acting this in an obedient hope,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Why have you suffer’d me to be imprison’d,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: Kept in a dark house, visited by the priest,

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: And made the most notorious geck and gull

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: That e’er invention played on? Tell me why?

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Alas, Malvolio, this is not my writing,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Though I confess, much like the character:

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: But out of question, ’tis Maria’s hand.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And now I do bethink me, it was she

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: First told me thou wast mad; then cam’st in smiling,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: And in such forms which here were presuppos’d

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Upon thee in the letter. Prithee, be content.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: This practice hath most shrewdly pass’d upon thee.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: But when we know the grounds and authors of it,

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Thou shalt be both the plaintiff and the judge

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Of thine own cause.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Good madam, hear me speak,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: And let no quarrel, nor no brawl to come,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Taint the condition of this present hour,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Which I have wonder’d at. In hope it shall not,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Most freely I confess, myself and Toby

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Set this device against Malvolio here,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: Upon some stubborn and uncourteous parts

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: We had conceiv’d against him. Maria writ

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: The letter, at Sir Toby’s great importance,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: In recompense whereof he hath married her.

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: How with a sportful malice it was follow’d

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: May rather pluck on laughter than revenge,

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: If that the injuries be justly weigh’d

lines.speaker: FABIAN
lines.text: That have on both sides passed.

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: Alas, poor fool, how have they baffled thee!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Why, ‘some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: greatness thrown upon them.’ I was one, sir, in this interlude, one Sir

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Topas, sir, but that’s all one. ‘By the Lord, fool, I am not mad.’ But

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: do you remember? ‘Madam, why laugh you at such a barren rascal? And you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: smile not, he’s gagged’? And thus the whirligig of time brings in his

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: revenges.

lines.speaker: MALVOLIO
lines.text: I’ll be revenged on the whole pack of you.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OLIVIA
lines.text: He hath been most notoriously abus’d.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Pursue him, and entreat him to a peace:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: He hath not told us of the captain yet.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: When that is known, and golden time convents,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A solemn combination shall be made

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of our dear souls.—Meantime, sweet sister,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: We will not part from hence.—Cesario, come:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For so you shall be while you are a man;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But when in other habits you are seen,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Orsino’s mistress, and his fancy’s queen.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Clown sings.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _   When that I was and a little tiny boy,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With hey, ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A foolish thing was but a toy,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For the rain it raineth every day._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _   But when I came to man’s estate,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With hey, ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Gainst knaves and thieves men shut their gate,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For the rain it raineth every day._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _   But when I came, alas, to wive,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With hey, ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: By swaggering could I never thrive,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For the rain it raineth every day._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _   But when I came unto my beds,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With hey, ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With toss-pots still had drunken heads,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For the rain it raineth every day._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _   A great while ago the world begun,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With hey, ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But that’s all one, our play is done,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And we’ll strive to please you every day._
[_Exit._]
